A.explanation: Force times displacement in the direction of the force is work done, $W = Fs$, which has magnitude only and is a scalar.

B.explanation: Mass is a scalar but acceleration is a vector, so $F = ma$ is a vector in the direction of the acceleration.

C.explanation: Pressure times area gives force, $F = pA$, which has direction normal to the area and is a vector.

D.explanation: Velocity is a vector and time is a scalar, so $s = vt$ is displacement which has direction and is a vector.

hints: Notice the wording in each product - decide whether each starting quantity is scalar with magnitude only or vector with magnitude and direction.
Recall that a scalar times a vector keeps the vector direction, while force times distance moved along the force gives work done in $\text{J}$.
Compare the four results - work done, force, force, and displacement - and pick the one with magnitude only and no direction.
walkthrough: List the nature of each quantity: force, displacement, acceleration, velocity are vectors, while mass, pressure, time are scalars.
Use the rule that scalar x vector gives a vector in the direction of the vector, but two vectors combined along the same line as in $W = Fs$ can give a scalar.
Check (force) x (displacement in direction of force): this is work done, measured in $\text{J}$, with magnitude only and no direction.
Check the others: (mass) x (acceleration) is force, (pressure) x (area) is force normal to the surface, (velocity) x (time) is displacement - all have direction so are vectors.
Only the work done product has no direction assigned to it, so it is the scalar quantity. This is option A.
